title: Existing tests that wrote a covers-less checkpoint now pass --covers
body:
**Chose:** in `a_checkpoint_records_the_slices_it_covers`, drop the `cp(&[])` assertion that a checkpoint without `--covers` is written with no covers field; give `the_board_reads_its_log_fields_from_log_jsonl` and the two log.rs unit tests (`ids_follow_their_sequence...`, `refusals_leave_the_file_unchanged`) explicit covers, and add a no-covers case to the unit refusal list.
**Over:** leaving them as they were, which goes red: they assert the very write FR-1 forbids.
**Because:** the PRD's acceptance makes a covers-less checkpoint write a refusal, so those assertions contradict an approved FR. The dropped assertion's behaviour is now asserted the other way round by `log_add_checkpoint_refuses_a_missing_covers`, which checks both an absent flag and an empty `--covers ""`. `a_log_without_covers_keeps_the_high_water_rule` is untouched.
**Undo:** restore the `cp(&[])` line and remove the covers arguments, after reverting the refusal in `validate()`.

title: How the pack prints a row's key and finds its Human? cell
body:
**Chose:** each handed row keeps its columns and gets `` key: `FR-6.1` `` after its closing pipe, plus `(deferred: Human? = yes)` on a human row; the `Human?` column is found by name in the table's header, the 4th cell when the header has none; the header printed is only the QA table's own contiguous lines, so another table's `|---` no longer leaks into it.
**Over:** a new leading Key column (changes the table's columns, which the slice keeps); always the 4th cell (wrong on a table with another column order).
**Because:** the slice fixes the key format but not where it prints; the worker reads raw text, and slice 04's contract line can point at the same `key:` token.
**Undo:** the `format!` and `human_col` lines in `qa_rows`, `src/pack.rs`.

title: The harness fixture's slices name their QA row in Prove
body:
**Chose:** `tests/harness/mod.rs` writes `` `prd.md` §8, the FR-1 row. `` under each fixture slice's `### 3. Prove` heading.
**Over:** leaving the fixture as scaffolded, which made seven `tests/checkpoints.rs` tests red (no `| FR-1` row in the pack, `**Prove:** none` from the stub).
**Because:** those tests relied on the whole-table fallback §5 removes; a slice that wants its row proven names it, which is the shape §5 now requires. No assertion changed.
**Undo:** drop the loop after `patch_prd_v3()` in the fixture setup.

title: Count the send-back by the checkpoint's own records, not by attempt
body:
**Chose:** the send-back cap counts the checkpoint entries numbered `n` or later (every one of them was written for this checkpoint and none was accepted, since `n` is max + 1); a record only counts as this worker's when that count grew during its run. The thin worker settles as `done`, so it never counts toward `DEATH_CAP`.
**Over:** capping on `attempt` as the slice says, which counts every worker this checkpoint spawned, dead and rate-limited ones included.
**Because:** with `attempt`, a worker that died followed by one short record would block with no send-back, folding deaths into the send-back count, which the slice's own trap forbids. The log count is also re-entrant from the board alone.
**Undo:** replace `records.len() < 2` with `attempt < 2` in `src/checkpoint.rs`.

title: The stub checkpoint worker takes a covers step key
body:
**Chose:** `tests/stubs/claude` gained a `covers: [n, ...]` step key on a checkpoint worker, naming the slices its record covers in place of every slice the pack hands it.
**Over:** a new fixture or a separate stub, or leaving the acceptance tests unwritten.
**Because:** the slice's acceptance needs a worker whose record names fewer slices than it was handed, and the stub had no way to write one; the file is outside the slice's listed files.
**Undo:** drop the key and the two tests that use it.

title: Which records the driver's view refuses, and where it is applied
body:
**Chose:** `checkpoint::accepted_only` refuses a record numbered from a checkpoint this run started and never finished (no `CheckpointDone`) up to the next one started, **unless** the record sits in `log.jsonl` after that checkpoint's last block: that record is the owner's answer and stands. A landing conflict on an accepted checkpoint record now emits `CheckpointDone { sha: None }` before its block (`block_conflict`). The view is applied in `src/scheduler.rs` through one `driver_board` helper, at the main loop's two board reads and in `closeout_owns`.
**Over:** the plain events rule the slice names, which refuses every record of an unfinished checkpoint.
**Because:** the plain rule breaks two existing paths. The death block's option 2 and the short-record block's option 2 tell the owner to write a record by hand and answer, and the plain rule would re-run the checkpoint over that record. The conflict block says "the run goes on past the recorded checkpoint", and the plain rule would re-run that one too. `scheduler.rs` is outside the slice's files, but it is where the driver decides that a checkpoint is due, and task 2 cannot be done anywhere else.
**Undo:** drop the `last_block` match in `accepted_only`, so every record in range is refused. Drop the `CheckpointDone` emit in `block_conflict`. Revert `driver_board` to `docs.status`.

title: The stub checkpoint worker writes one evidence dir per key
body:
**Chose:** `tests/stubs/claude` writes `cp-<n>/<key>/proof.txt` for every handed key not marked deferred. It also takes an `evidence: {"<key>": "absent"|"empty"|"link"|"file"}` step key, and its record's `**Prove:**` line gains `— rows: <key>: <path>, …` (`0 rows handed` when the pack hands none). It still writes `cp-<n>/row.txt`.
**Over:** a separate stub, or acceptance tests that cannot leave a row's dir missing.
**Because:** the acceptance tests need a worker that skips a row, leaves it empty or puts a link in its place. Without per-key dirs, every existing checkpoint test would block. `row.txt` and the old Prove prefix stay, so `checkpoint_evidence_lands_in_the_run_dir_and_never_in_the_branch` is unchanged.
**Undo:** drop the `keyed` loop and the `evidence` key from the stub, then delete the tests that use it.

title: A record written after a checkpoint block's answer is a worker's, not the owner's
body:
**Chose:** `checkpoint::accepted_only` keeps a record from an unfinished checkpoint only when it sits after the checkpoint's last block **and before that block's answer** (or the block is unanswered). A record after the answer is refused like any other record of the unfinished checkpoint.
**Over:** AD-6 as built, which keeps every record after the last block. A checkpoint resumed under the same `n` after a red-gate or death block can have its worker write a short record, be sent back, and then stop (`factory stop`, a budget hold); the next driver would read that worker's record as the owner's and count the rejected slices as verified, with no evidence ever checked.
**Because:** both owner flows the blocks describe (death block option 2, short-record block option 2) add the record and then answer, so the answer is the boundary between the owner's record and a resumed worker's. Found by the second-opinion fallback in polish; pinned by `a_record_after_the_blocks_answer_is_a_workers_and_is_refused`.
**Undo:** drop the `answer.is_some_and(|a| r > a)` term in `accepted_only`, `src/checkpoint.rs`. An owner who answers first and writes the record after now sees the checkpoint re-run rather than accept it.

title: A checkpoint worker left by a killed driver lands only on a record the driver would accept
body:
**Chose:** `settle_checkpoint_orphan` (`src/scheduler.rs`) lands an earlier driver's checkpoint worker only when `checkpoint::orphan_record_holds` passes: the newest record numbered `n` or later covers the `CheckpointStarted`/`CheckpointResumed` covers, and every row `pack::handed_qa` recomputes for those covers has its evidence. A worker that left a record short of either is settled `done` and the checkpoint runs again under the next number.
**Over:** landing on any `CP-n` (the old rule), which emitted `CheckpointDone` for a thin record, so `accepted_only` then counted it and the send-back and evidence checks never ran after a driver restart.
**Because:** a restart mid-checkpoint is the one path where the new checks were skipped. `handed_qa` is now the single place the handed rows come from, used by `Pack::for_checkpoint` too, so the orphan check cannot drift from the live one. Pinned by `a_short_record_left_by_a_killed_driver_does_not_close_the_checkpoint`.
**Undo:** restore `lands = w.role == "fix" || (w.role == "checkpoint" && board.checkpoints.iter().any(|c| c.n == n))` and drop the short-record branch below it.

title: A Human? cell reads yes by its first word
body:
**Chose:** a row is deferred when its `Human?` cell's first word, after leading `*`/`_`, is `yes` in any case: `yes`, `**yes**: routing is judgment`, `yes → qa-guide.md`.
**Over:** an exact `yes` match, which treated those cells as owing evidence. Five archived PRDs in this repo write the cell that way, so the last checkpoint of such a feature would send back and block on rows no worker can prove — the case PRD §4 excludes.
**Because:** the PRD says "a row marked `Human? = yes`" without fixing the cell's exact text, and the repo's own tables annotate the yes. Pinned by `a_human_cell_reads_yes_by_its_first_word`.
**Undo:** replace `is_yes(c)` with `c.eq_ignore_ascii_case("yes")` in `qa_rows`, `src/pack.rs`.
